input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights". That is walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT: it is multi-year, has no 12-month limit, no reduction on notice, and no true-up in place of a shortfall penalty, so it fails the fallback on every material term. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment", and sits uneasily with Section 7.1 (Fees are those stated in each Order Form, with no unidentified minimum-use charge). We therefore replaced 2.1 with the preferred position — no minimum purchase or volume commitment and payment only for Services used or ordered — which also removes the internal conflict with 12.3. No other clause imposes a volume floor or usage cap on Customer.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year USD 2,000,000 take-or-pay commitment and confirm payment for usage or ordered Services only.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, and it contradicts Section 12.3's acknowledgement that we have made no minimum-volume commitment. We replaced it with our preferred position that we pay only for Services used or ordered; if a commitment is essential, we could discuss one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up rather than a penalty.
